research_document.summary: Confirmed: the CURRENT manual-approval threshold is defined by finance revision F-2024-11, in the final block of billing-policy/src/policy/refunds.py — NOT the superseded history at the file head. Exact anchors: line 205 `# CURRENT policy — finance revision F-2024-11 (effective 2024-03-01).`; lines 216-217 `#: The CURRENT manual-approval threshold (F-2024-11): refunds at or above this amount require a human approval step before capture.`; line 218 `REFUND_MANUAL_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 5000` (i.e., $50.00); line 221 `REFUND_POLICY_VERSION = "F-2024-11"`; line 230 `return int(amount_cents) >= REFUND_MANUAL_APPROVAL_THRESHOLD_CENTS` (inclusive 'at or above' comparison). Exact window: effective 2024-03-01, no end date — currently in force. README.md:7 confirms 'The CURRENT refund approval policy (revision F-2024-11)' and README.md:9 marks the earlier sections as superseded history kept only for statement reconciliation. The superseded revisions were excluded as instructed: F-2023-04 ol
assumptions: 5000 cents equals $50.00 USD (module names the constant in cents)
The threshold is inclusive: refunds 'at or above' 5000 cents require the human approval step, per refunds.py:216-217 and the >= comparison at refunds.py:230
Effective window '2024-03-01' has no stated end date, so F-2024-11 is the rule in force today
contradictions: None. The file-head history (F-2023 / F-2024-02) states different ceilings but is explicitly marked DEPRECATED/SUPERSEDED (refunds.py:144, 168, 176) and README.md:9, so it does not contradict the current F-2024-11 rule.
research_document.rules: Bounded research pass over the authorized snapshot. complete=false means a budget stopped the investigation early — the findings are partial, not exhaustive. Findings cite evidence:<id> recorded by this discovery. tokens.input/output are the EXACT totals only when unknown_usage_calls is 0; otherwise the *_lower_bound fields are what was actually observed.
